name: Vannam

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A senior Kandyan dance master with deep knowledge of the traditional repertoire.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Vannam originated as recitations ('varnana') and were later adapted into solo dances.
Their development was significantly encouraged by King Sri Weeraparakrama Narendrasinghe (1707-1739).
The lyrics for the eighteen principal Vannam were composed by the sage Ganithalankara.

narration: Vannam are performed as solo dances.
The dancer uses movements and gestures to describe the behavior of the subject, such as animals or deities, while the accompanying song provides the narrative background.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music features the Geta Bera (a tapered, hand-played drum) and Thalampataa (cymbals).
The rhythm is central, and the dancer performs to the song's lyrics.
Listen for the Geta Bera, Thalampataa.
The music is defined by the rhythmic beating of the Geta Bera drum and the metallic punctuation of the Thalampataa cymbals, accompanying vocal poetry that narrates the movements of the dancer.

scenes.title: The people
narration: King Sri Weeraparakrama Narendrasinghe and the sage Ganithalankara are the primary figures associated with the formalization of the eighteen Vannam.
There are eighteen classical Vannam, with later additions including the Samanala (butterfly), Mahabo (sacred bo tree), and Hansa (swan) Vannam.
Vannam belongs to the Kandyan dance (Uda Rata Natum) tradition of Sri Lanka.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: The music is defined by the rhythmic beating of the Geta Bera drum and the metallic punctuation of the Thalampataa cymbals, accompanying vocal poetry that narrates the movements of the dancer.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Vannam (Sri Lanka). Instruments: Geta Bera, Thalampataa. Vocal style: Poetry sung to music (kavi). Form: Descriptive song accompanying solo dance. Mood: expressive, descriptive, rhythmic. It should sound like this: The music is defined by the rhythmic beating of the Geta Bera drum and the metallic punctuation of the Thalampataa cymbals, accompanying vocal poetry that narrates the movements of the dancer. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress with a respectful nod (palette and fabric only): the sources describe sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire, or the dance is sacred
wardrobe.from_sources: Performances traditionally took place in a 'kavikara maduwa', a decorated dance arena. The full 'ves' costume is only awarded to dancers who have mastered all eighteen Vannam.
care: every element traceable to the costume notes or a licensed image; nothing added for effect
no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
credits name the tradition and the sources of the reconstruction
